## 固定收益開篇主論

5月28日公布的一系列美國數據顯示，家庭所得轉弱、基礎資本支出放緩、第1季經濟成長下修，新屋銷售也明顯不如預期，帶動美國公債全線上漲。10年期殖利率下跌3.6個基點至4.448%，30年期下跌3.9個基點至4.974%；相較之下，2年期僅下跌1.1個基點至4.023%。殖利率曲線因此呈多頭趨平，2年與10年期利差收窄2.5個基點至42.5個基點。

這波漲勢並非明確的通膨降溫訊號。4月核心個人消費支出（PCE）物價較3月上漲0.2%，低於預期，但整體與核心通膨年增率仍分別達3.8%及3.3%。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams認為政策略具限制性，目前適合等待更多資訊；聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem則表示，實質政策利率低於中性水準，官員仍須保留升息可能。期貨定價顯示，年底前升息的機率超過50%。

美債行情的組成正反映這項矛盾。10年期實質殖利率下跌3.5個基點至2.033%，幾乎與名目殖利率的跌幅相同，10年期損益兩平通膨率則僅下滑0.1個基點至2.415%。投資人調降了實質利率壓力，卻未大幅下修市場的通膨溢價。長端同時順利吸收$440億的7年期公債標售，得標最高殖利率為4.290%，間接投標人占獲配競爭性投標的78.39%。

風險資產與政府債券同步上漲。標普500指數上漲約0.58%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.84%，半導體指數上漲1.00%，VIX則下跌3.38%。布蘭特原油下跌0.62%至$93.71，單週跌幅達8.65%，降低眼前的能源價格衝擊；不過，各國央行仍將戰爭引發的通膨及其第二輪效應視為實際存在的政策風險。

## 需求數據轉弱，聯準會辯論轉鷹

4月所得與支出報告的通膨及家庭所得細節均有利於存續期間部位。個人所得較3月持平，低於0.4%的市場共識，前值為成長0.5%；可支配個人所得則下滑0.1%。名目消費成長0.5%，符合預期，但低於先前的1.0%，實質支出僅增加0.1%。個人儲蓄率由2.9%降至2.6%，顯示家庭在所得未同步增加之際，仍維持名目支出。

整體PCE物價月增0.4%，低於0.5%的市場共識，也較前值0.7%放緩；核心物價上漲0.2%，同樣低於預期0.1個百分點，並低於先前的0.3%。單月數據的威脅程度不如市場原先擔心，但整體與核心通膨年增率仍分別達3.8%及3.3%，遠高於聯準會目標。

第1季GDP第2次估值也強化經濟成長轉弱的訊號。實質GDP年化成長率由初值2.0%下修至1.6%，原先市場共識亦為2.0%；下修主要來自投資與消費支出較弱。實質國內所得成長0.9%，低於第4季的1.6%，GDP與國內所得的平均成長率則為1.2%。

製造業訂單的表面數字強勁，內部表現卻明顯分歧。受運輸設備訂單激增21.5%帶動，4月耐久財訂單大增7.9%，不但超過3.9%共識的兩倍，也高於3月經修正後的1.3%。扣除運輸項目的訂單仍成長1.1%，但扣除飛機的非國防資本財訂單下跌1.1%。換言之，由飛機訂單推高的整體數字，並未延伸至最能反映企業基礎設備需求的項目。

利率敏感的房市則呈現較一致的疲弱。4月新建單戶住宅銷售下跌6.2%，年化為62.2萬戶，低於66萬戶的市場共識及3月經修正後的66.3萬戶；銷售量較一年前減少11.3%，可售庫存則由8.7個月增至9.4個月，銷售價格中位數為$42.25萬。成交減少而庫存增加，相較於耐久財整體數字，更清楚顯示高融資成本正在壓抑需求。

首次申領失業救濟人數也傳達較溫和的轉弱訊號。截至5月23日當週，申領人數由經修正後的21萬增至21.5萬，高於21.1萬的市場共識；4週移動平均由經修正後的20.275萬升至20.9萬。數據顯示勞動市場邊際降溫，但惡化程度尚不足以單獨壓過通膨疑慮。

當日聯準會官員的談話同樣反映宏觀情勢的多空交錯。身為紐約聯準銀行總裁及FOMC常任投票委員的Williams表示，3.5%至3.75%的政策利率區間略具限制性，也足以因應伊朗衝突的影響。他預期戰爭與關稅推升物價的速度將在未來數月觸頂，使決策者有時間評估數據，並認為基礎勞動市場表現良好。

Williams將這項短期判斷與生產力分析分開看待。結構性生產力改善可在薪資與物價調整期間暫時壓低通膨，但最終應會提高經通膨調整後的利率。他主要提醒，這類變化很難即時辨識，其持續時間與影響也過於不確定，不能據以判斷近期政策利率走向。

Musalem從同一場生產力辯論得出更偏緊縮的政策結論。他表示，官員不應依賴未來可能出現的人工智慧生產力提升來化解當前通膨，尤其依其判斷，實質政策利率低於FOMC估計的長期中性水準。他並指出，通膨仍顯著高於目標，長期通膨預期逐步上升，而勞動市場保持穩定。

Musalem也明確列出考慮升息的條件：若未來一至兩季未能恢復通膨降溫趨勢，或通膨預期持續處於高檔甚至進一步上升，他將感到憂慮。他贊同在4月政策聲明中移除寬鬆傾向的官員，並表示考慮升息的機率不能是零。他估計，近期美債殖利率上升約四分之三反映市場上調預期中性政策利率，僅四分之一來自期限溢價。

Williams與Musalem的分歧不在於通膨是否重要，而是現行政策容許決策者保持多少耐心。Williams認為政策略具限制性，且價格衝擊可能觸頂；Musalem則認為實質利率低於中性水準，也沒有充分證據顯示生產力能帶來不伴隨通膨的成長。6月17日至18日的會議將是主席Kevin Warsh上任後首次主持，屆時這場辯論將反映在政策聲明與新一輪經濟預測之中。

## 標售需求與充裕資金支撐利率市場

美國財政部標售$440億新發行7年期公債，得標最高殖利率為4.290%，投標倍數為2.52倍。間接投標人占獲配競爭性投標的78.39%，直接投標人占11.19%，一級交易商占10.42%；財政部在最高殖利率價位分配了該價位投標量的71.23%。這批公債預定於6月1日交割。

中期券種周邊交易相當活躍。名目附息美債的申報面額交易量較前一交易日增加11.9%至$1.246兆；超過5年、最長7年的券種交易量增加66.0%至$1,285億，其中指標新券占81.9%。這些總量衡量的是周轉，而非需求方向，但足以顯示標售與整體漲勢伴隨的交易規模。

本次供給是在資金異常充裕的融資環境中獲得吸收。5月約有$1,200億流入貨幣市場基金，附買回利率低於聯準會目標區間下限；有效聯邦資金利率當月兩度下移，擔保隔夜融資利率（SOFR）則略高於3.50%，4月平均約為3.65%。

這種寬鬆情勢部分源自4月報稅季前後國庫券供給減少逾$2,700億，以及財政部的現金管理買回操作，使大量現金競逐擔保品。不過，多家銀行的策略師認為，寬鬆情勢延續太久，無法單以季節因素解釋。

強化補充槓桿比率規則的調整，擴大了大型銀行中介美債與附買回部位的能力。部分銀行在4月1日截止日前便採用新規，使交易商即使持有的美債庫存在3月底升至創紀錄的$5,570億，仍有能力承接。自2025年6月資產上限解除後，富國銀行也成為附買回融資的重要邊際供應者。

銀行資產負債表擴張幅度相當可觀。第1季，美國8家全球系統性重要銀行的總資產合計增加$1.3兆，其中附賣回交易增加$3,000億，證券部位增加約$4,000億，包括美債交易簿的$1,000億。額外的中介能力有助解釋，為何交易商持有大量庫存，卻未重現去年所見的融資壓力。

融資利率若持續偏低，可能影響聯準會的準備金管理購買。官員已將每月國庫券購買規模由4月以前的$400億及5月的$250億，降至約$100億。紐約聯準銀行市場主管Roberto Perli表示，購買速度可依市場情況調整；策略師則提出，若隔夜融資持續異常寬鬆，聯準會可能暫停購買。

目前的融資環境不只是美債漲勢的技術性背景。較低的附買回成本讓交易商更容易為大量庫存融資並吸收供給；銀行資產負債表容量若能持久擴大，也會降低例行發債突然造成擔保品或準備金緊縮的機率。6月的現金管理操作將是檢驗結構性與季節性力量如何交互作用的下一項測試。

## 信用需求強勁，但選擇性日益提高

歐洲銀行正利用偏緊的風險溢價，延長額外第一類資本債（AT1）首次可贖回前的期間。2026年主要幣別AT1發行中，首次可贖回日為10年的債券占四分之一，在傳統標準首次贖回期為5年的市場中，這一比重前所未見。

Banco Santander發行$15億的10年不可贖回AT1；NatWest則發行£5億、可於2036年贖回且票息7.5%的證券。德意志銀行、法國巴黎銀行與瑞銀今年也發行了長贖回期結構。由於5年與10年期之間的利差曲線相對平坦，新增的大部分利率曝險又可透過交換交易處理，銀行得以約300個基點的利差取得約10年的第一類資本融資。

對投資人而言，這類結構承擔的存續期間與流動性風險高於傳統5年可贖回債券。若市場利率上升，長贖回期AT1的跌幅可能更大；其次級市場規模較小，承壓時也可能更快失去流動性。偏緊的新券利差對重新定價提供的緩衝同樣較少。不過，銀行股權價值若改善，延長贖回期也可能帶來更大的上漲空間，因為債券價格較不會受到近期按面額贖回預期的緊密約束。

能與主權政治風險隔離的新興市場借款人也獲得需求支持。2026年前5個月，阿根廷各省與布宜諾斯艾利斯市合計發債$23億，為2017年以來同期最高。布宜諾斯艾利斯市發行$5億10年期債券，殖利率7.4%，是該市歷來最低借款成本，認購金額約達$30億。

科爾多瓦省以8.95%發行$8億，丘布特省則以9.45%籌得$6.5億，兩者都利用市場進行債務再融資及延長到期日；丘布特省並以石油權利金收入為債券提供擔保。恩特雷里奧斯省睽違近10年首度重返國際市場，以9.6%完成$3億交易。

省級債市讓投資人得以把較強的地方信用或有擔保的收入來源，與聯邦政府面臨的選舉風險區隔開來。阿根廷主權政府並未在接近9%的殖利率下赴海外發債，而是繼續依賴短期本地債務及附買回融資。2027年大選前到期的本地主權美元債殖利率約為5.1%，大選後到期債券則約為8.6%。

不過，這種區隔並不完整。各省通常需要取得央行提供的美元，才能償付外幣債務；過去的主權危機也曾迅速蔓延至地方發行人。省級債務在2001年崩盤及2020年危機期間均曾重整；2020年時，布宜諾斯艾利斯省幾乎重組了全部$71億的違約債券。

私募市場的另一項趨勢是，大型擬議融資愈來愈依賴結構性信用保障，而非借款人自身的獲利能力。Apollo與Blackstone正為約$360億債務融資尋找更多投資人，資金將用於購買Anthropic租用的晶片，以在紐約、德州、路易斯安那州及印第安納州建置人工智慧基礎設施。

一個特殊目的機構將購買Google設計的張量處理器，並收取Anthropic支付的租金。融資預計包括約$60億A1票據、$250億A2票據及$45億B票據，但金額仍可能調整。交易採延後動撥結構，可隨晶片到貨及租約生效逐步投入資金。

協助Google開發晶片的Broadcom將為優先順位A1及A2票據提供殘值支持。若Anthropic在約定期間內停止支付租金，特殊目的機構將出售晶片；若所得不足以全額償付這些優先投資人，Broadcom將補足差額。這使優先票據的信用特性與Broadcom的投資等級信用相連，次順位B票據則在償付結構中排於其後。

這項保障至關重要，因為Anthropic目前尚未產生足以獨力支撐如此龐大債務的獲利。該公司另行宣布以$9,650億估值進行$650億股權募資。Apollo與Blackstone計畫保留相當大部分的融資，再將其餘部位分銷給其他投資人；交易於當週徵求認購，預計下一週完成。

相較之下，軟體業再融資面臨的情況截然不同。即使Thoma Bravo為資安公司Sophos提出的$25億再融資案，指示利差已提高至接近基準利率加600個基點，多家私募信貸公司仍拒絕參與。Sophos現有債務的利差約為350個基點，其中包括一筆2027年3月到期的$21億貸款。

因此，Thoma Bravo正考慮與高盛同步推動修改條款並延長期限的方案。現有貸款人要求贊助方追加股本、償還部分債務並提高定價，作為將到期日延長約2.5年的交換條件。Thoma Bravo目前已在該公司投入逾$23億股本。

標普全球評級最近將Sophos一家實體的展望調降至負向，並表示若未能在兩個月內為即將到期的債務完成再融資，評級可能遭到下調。Sophos貸款價格接近面額的97美分；公司在截至12月的季度產生自由現金流，年度經常性收入約為$13.4億。這些營運與市場指標提供一定支撐，但緊迫的再融資時程已形成流動性限制。

貸款人的抗拒也反映市場正更廣泛地重新評估軟體業曝險，考量人工智慧是否會削弱既有訂閱制業務。部分企業發展公司已開始出售特定軟體貸款，另一些投資人則買進折價部位。Anthropic與Sophos兩案的差異顯示，當交易結構可將關鍵風險轉移至財務實力更強的主體時，市場對科技相關私募債務的需求仍然龐大；但若貸款人必須直接承擔借款人的再融資及產業顛覆風險，資金便不再理所當然地進場。

Jefferies另一起爭議則凸顯低流動性信用資產的法律與擔保品風險。Leucadia Asset Management旗下352 Capital基金的投資人提出擬議集體訴訟，指稱該基金明知擔保品並不存在，且前投資組合經理Jordan Chirico在Water Station Management擁有個人投資，仍持續買進該公司債券。

Jefferies指控Chirico就其投資及與Water Station的關係誤導公司。Chirico遭控詐欺後不認罪，並透過律師表示，自己是所指控騙局的受害者，而非組織者。投資人訴狀要求金額未定的賠償，並指稱債券文件中的保障條款遭到豁免，包括與擔保品陳述及財務報告相關的違約事件。這些內容目前仍屬指控，並非司法裁定的事實。

## 央行正面迎戰能源衝擊

歐洲央行4月29日至30日會議紀要顯示，多名官員認為當時的決策相當接近；如果有人正式提議升息，他們不會反對。此後，包括部分通常被視為管理委員會鴿派的官員在內，決策者均暗示6月可能升息。

歐元區通膨率為3%，官員擔心能源成本上升可能傳導至薪資要求及長期通膨預期。歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，即使最初的能源衝擊逆轉，其第二輪效應仍會持續一段時間。經濟學家與投資人預期2026年至少升息兩次。

南非已立即採取行動。南非準備銀行將基準利率上調25個基點至7%，是2023年以來首次升息，也符合受訪19位經濟學家中18人的預測。由6人組成的委員會以4票對2票通過升息，兩名委員主張維持不變；會中也曾討論升息50個基點。

總裁Lesetja Kganyago表示，通膨風險加劇及多重衝擊交疊，可能引發第二輪效應。央行設想的3種戰爭情境都顯示政策仍須進一步緊縮，其中最不利情境下，政策利率將在第3季升至7.83%。央行把2026年通膨預測由3.7%上調至4.4%，經濟成長預估由1.4%下修至1.2%，季度模型中的年底利率預測則由6.47%提高至6.7%。

燃料價格升至近4年高點後，南非4月通膨率由3.1%加速至4.0%，創20個月新高。約翰尼斯堡尾盤，南非幣在回吐早先部分漲幅後，兌美元仍升值約0.2%至16.327；10年期政府債殖利率則扭轉稍早升勢，降至8.62%，較盤中高點低9個基點。

巴西則在重新評估寬鬆循環能否持續。央行貨幣政策主管Nilton David指出，在央行連續兩次降息25個基點後，2028年通膨預期進一步惡化。5月上旬年通膨率加速至4.64%，部分經濟學家預期，央行最快可能在6月暫停降息，屆時Selic利率將維持在14.5%。

David表示，貨幣政策對2026年通膨的影響有限，但仍有時間讓2028年通膨預期回到3%目標附近。他的談話清楚表明，降息不代表政策已不再具限制性；央行也不會允許外部能源衝擊延續至相關政策期間以外，目前該期間設定為2027年第4季。

## 歐洲與日本重新定價主權債券利率風險

隨著各國政府面對國防、基礎設施與能源轉型成本，歐洲共同舉債的討論正逐漸成為財政政策核心。16個成員國在5月下旬簽署文件，要求考慮透過新的共同舉債，為歐洲投資及公共財相關貸款提供資金；文件也主張放緩疫情復甦債務的償還進度，該債務預定自2028年起開始償付。

法國、西班牙與希臘普遍支持擴大共同發債，德國與荷蘭仍對財政義務共同化抱持疑慮。歐盟執委會已提議推出以共同舉債融資的特定工具，包括最高€4,000億的危機機制。波蘭支持為國防共同舉債，德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel也表示，部分國家層級的舉債能力可移轉至歐盟層級。

尚未清償的疫情復甦機制債務超過€8,000億，歐盟另已同意向烏克蘭提供由歐盟預算支持的€900億貸款。2025年通過的國防貸款計畫，已允許歐盟執委會先行借款，再貸給各國政府，償還義務仍由個別成員國承擔。

共同發債規模若足夠大，可在德國公債之外建立更具深度的歐元區安全資產市場，擴大銀行的主權債曝險配置，並為民間借款提供流動性更高的定價基準。另一種選項是以主權債券為擔保的證券，將各國債務集中作為擔保品，切分成不同風險及殖利率的分層，而不增加共同承擔的義務。兩種方式都必須具備足夠發行量，才能形成實質流動性；永久性共同舉債則仍須取得目前尚不存在的政治共識。

日本已經顯示，主權債殖利率結構性上升會如何重塑整個金融體系。10年期日本政府公債殖利率自2008年以來首次超過東證股價指數的股息殖利率；日本公司債殖利率也升至相關指數自2000年編製以來最高水準，使企業在舊債到期時面臨更高的再融資成本。

市場已不再只把這波走勢解讀為日本央行2024年結束負利率後的良性正常化。大和證券估計，自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，10年期日本政府公債的期限溢價已上升近70個基點。殖利率上升之際，日圓反而走弱，顯示投資人更重視通膨、財政擴張與政府供給增加，而非單純認為日本資產報酬改善。

美國收盤後、亞洲早晨公布的東京通膨數據，使日本央行6月決策更為複雜。5月扣除生鮮食品的消費者物價較一年前上漲1.3%，是4年來最慢增幅，並連續第6個月減速；扣除生鮮食品與能源的通膨率為1.6%，整體CPI則為1.4%。

政府補貼及自來水服務費大幅下降壓低了物價指數。服務價格上漲1.1%，扣除生鮮食品的食物價格上漲4.1%；米價下跌1.0%，為2022年8月以來首次下降。4月工業生產意外增加，零售銷售較3月增強，失業率則降至2.5%。

這些結果雖緩和當前通膨情勢，卻未消除日本央行面對的油價、匯率與財政風險。交易員認為，6月15日至16日會議升息25個基點的機率約為77%。日圓兌美元約報159.31，接近4月30日匯市干預以來最弱水準；已公布的8月食品漲價計畫則顯示，成本轉嫁壓力仍將延續。

## 後市意義

美國下一項經濟成長資訊將是5月29日公布的4月先期經濟指標。市場共識預估，商品貿易逆差為$865億，前值為$879億；零售庫存預計成長0.4%，批發庫存成長0.8%。第1季GDP下修後，這些數據將影響即時追蹤預測。

6月1日公布的ISM製造業調查，將檢驗4月指數錄得52.7後，擴張是否延續。新訂單及就業分項有助判斷核心資本財訂單的疲弱是否擴大；支付價格則可顯示能源衝擊是否正傳導至工業投入成本。

接下來的勞動市場資訊將更為詳細。6月2日公布的4月JOLTS報告，將更新職缺、聘僱及離職數據；先前初值顯示職缺為686.6萬個。6月3日美東時間08:15將公布5月ADP報告，前值為增加10.9萬人；在首次申領失業救濟人數升至21.5萬後，6月4日還將公布下一期數據。這些指標合併觀察，可判斷最新的申領人數上升只是雜訊，還是勞動市場流動開始轉弱。

PCE公布後，6月3日ISM服務業調查將是更重要的成長與通膨交叉驗證。整體指數前值為53.6，但對正在考慮是否移除寬鬆傾向的聯準會而言，就業與支付價格分項最為重要。當日稍晚公布的褐皮書，則將在6月17日至18日FOMC會議前，提供各地區的需求、聘僱、信用狀況及物價壓力證據。

財政部操作也將檢驗異常寬鬆的融資環境。6月3日美東時間13:40至14:00的流動性支持買回，最多可能接受$20億、期限20年至30年的名目附息公債，並於6月4日交割。6月4日的現金管理買回，則最多可能接受$125億、期限1個月至2年的名目附息公債，於6月5日交割。前者是既定的長天期流動性操作；後者對短期擔保品供給及資金充裕的附買回市場有更直接的影響。

overall_summary.headline: 需求轉弱壓低實質殖利率，美債上漲、曲線趨平，但通膨疑慮未消
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債全線上漲，長天期券種領漲。10年期殖利率下跌3.6個基點至4.448%，30年期下跌3.9個基點至4.974%，2年期則下跌1.1個基點至4.023%。2年與10年期利差收窄2.5個基點至42.5個基點。

家庭所得轉弱、第1季經濟成長下修、核心資本財訂單疲弱及新屋銷售明顯不如預期，共同推動這波行情。核心PCE月增率也以0.2%低於預期，但整體及核心通膨年增率仍分別高達3.8%與3.3%。10年期名目殖利率的跌幅幾乎全由實質殖利率貢獻，損益兩平通膨率則大致持平，顯示市場主要反映實質利率壓力降低，而非大幅下修通膨溢價。$440億7年期公債標售需求強勁，進一步強化漲勢。

聯準會官員對前景提出不同解讀。John Williams認為政策略具限制性，目前適合耐心等待；Alberto Musalem則主張實質政策利率低於中性水準，並保留升息選項。期貨顯示年底前升息的機率超過50%。股債齊揚、波動率下降，布蘭特原油的單週跌幅緩和了眼前的能源衝擊，但第二輪通膨疑慮仍未消除。
overall_summary.summary: 所得、基礎投資、房市及第1季成長同步轉弱，拉低10年期與30年期美債殖利率；但年通膨仍具黏性，聯準會內部看法分歧，使這波漲勢未能成為明確的通膨降溫訊號。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied across the curve on May 28 as a dense U.S. data slate showed softer household income, weaker underlying capital spending, slower first-quarter growth and a pronounced miss in new-home sales. The 10-year yield fell 3.6 basis points to 4.448% and the 30-year declined 3.9 basis points to 4.974%, compared with a 1.1-basis-point drop in the 2-year yield to 4.023%. That bull-flattening left the 2s10s curve at 42.5 basis points, 2.5 basis points narrower on the day.

The rally did not amount to a clean disinflation signal. April core personal consumption expenditures prices rose a softer-than-expected 0.2% from March, but headline inflation still ran at 3.8% from a year earlier and core inflation at 3.3%. New York Fed President John Williams judged policy slightly restrictive and well placed to wait for more information, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the real policy rate was below neutral and that officials needed to remain open to an increase. Futures pricing assigned more than a 50% probability to a rate increase by year-end.

The composition of the Treasury move reflected that tension. The 10-year real yield fell 3.5 basis points to 2.033%, almost matching the nominal-yield decline, while the 10-year breakeven slipped only 0.1 basis point to 2.415%. Investors marked down real-rate pressure without materially revising the market inflation premium. The long end also absorbed a $44 billion 7-year auction that stopped at 4.290%, with indirect bidders taking 78.39% of accepted competitive bids.

Risk assets advanced alongside government bonds. The S&P 500 gained about 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.84% and the semiconductor index added 1.00%, while the VIX fell 3.38%. Brent declined 0.62% to $93.71 and was down 8.65% over the week, reducing the immediate energy impulse even as central banks continued to treat war-related inflation and second-round effects as live policy risks.

## Softer Demand Data Meets a Harder Fed Debate

The April income and spending report offered support for duration through both its inflation and household-income details. Personal income was unchanged from March, missing the 0.4% consensus after a 0.5% increase previously, while disposable personal income fell 0.1%. Nominal consumption rose 0.5%, matching expectations but slowing from 1.0%, and real spending increased only 0.1%. The personal saving rate fell to 2.6% from 2.9%, showing that households maintained nominal expenditure without a corresponding rise in income.

Headline PCE prices increased 0.4% on the month, below the 0.5% consensus and down from 0.7%. Core prices rose 0.2%, also one-tenth below expectations and slower than the prior 0.3%. Those monthly readings were less threatening than feared, but the annual rates remained far above the Federal Reserve’s objective: 3.8% for headline inflation and 3.3% for core.

The second estimate of first-quarter GDP reinforced the softer growth side of the picture. Real GDP was revised to a 1.6% annualized increase from the 2.0% advance estimate, which had also been the consensus. Weaker investment and consumer spending accounted for most of the revision. Real gross domestic income rose 0.9%, down from 1.6% in the fourth quarter, while the average of GDP and GDI increased 1.2%.

Manufacturing orders delivered a superficially stronger but internally divided result. Durable-goods orders jumped 7.9% in April, more than double the 3.9% consensus and up from a revised 1.3% increase in March, as transportation-equipment orders surged 21.5%. Orders excluding transportation still rose 1.1%, but nondefense capital-goods orders excluding aircraft fell 1.1%. The aircraft-heavy headline therefore did not carry through to the component most closely associated with underlying business-equipment demand.

Rate-sensitive housing was weaker more uniformly. New single-family home sales fell 6.2% in April to a 622,000 annualized pace, below the 660,000 consensus and a revised 663,000 in March. Sales were 11.3% lower than a year earlier, while available inventory increased to 9.4 months of supply from 8.7 months. The median sales price was $422,500. The combination of lower turnover and more inventory gave the bond market a clearer sign of restraint from elevated financing costs than the durable-goods headline did.

Initial jobless claims offered a milder version of the same message. Claims rose to 215,000 in the week ended May 23 from a revised 210,000, exceeding the 211,000 consensus. The four-week average increased to 209,000 from a revised 202,750. The figures showed some softening at the margin, but not the kind of deterioration that would by itself override the inflation concern.

That mixed macro picture was reflected in the day’s Federal Reserve communication. Williams, a permanent FOMC voter as New York Fed president, said the 3.5%-3.75% policy range was exerting a slightly restrictive effect and was well positioned to respond to the consequences of the Iran conflict. He expected the pace of war- and tariff-related price increases to peak over coming months, giving policymakers time to assess the data, and described the underlying labor market as doing well.

Williams separated that near-term judgment from his analysis of productivity. Structural productivity improvements can temporarily lower inflation as wages and prices adjust, but they should eventually raise inflation-adjusted interest rates. His central caution was that such shifts are unusually difficult to identify in real time, making their duration and implications too uncertain to support a near-term policy-rate call.

Musalem drew a more restrictive policy conclusion from the same productivity debate. The St. Louis Fed president said officials should not rely on prospective artificial-intelligence gains to solve current inflation, particularly when the real policy rate was, in his assessment, below the FOMC’s estimate of long-run neutral. He also pointed to inflation meaningfully above target, longer-run expectations drifting upward and a stable labor market.

His conditions for considering a rate increase were explicit. Musalem said he would become concerned if disinflation did not resume over the next one or two quarters, or if inflation expectations remained elevated or continued to rise. He agreed with officials who wanted to remove the easing bias from the April policy statement and said the probability of considering an increase had to be greater than zero. He estimated that roughly three-quarters of the recent rise in Treasury yields reflected a higher expected neutral policy rate, with only one-quarter coming from term premium.

The distinction between Williams and Musalem was therefore not whether inflation mattered, but how much patience current policy afforded. Williams saw a slightly restrictive stance and the prospect that the price shock would peak; Musalem saw a real rate below neutral and insufficient evidence that productivity would deliver noninflationary growth. The June 17-18 meeting, the first led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, will force that debate into the statement and the new economic projections.

## Auction Demand and Abundant Cash Support the Rates Market

Treasury’s $44 billion new 7-year note stopped at a 4.290% high yield with a 2.52 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received 78.39% of accepted competitive bids, direct bidders 11.19% and primary dealers 10.42%. Treasury allotted 71.23% of bids tendered at the high yield. The note is due to settle on June 1.

Trading activity was elevated around the intermediate sector. Reported par activity in nominal Treasury coupons rose 11.9% from the previous session to $1.246 trillion. Activity in maturities longer than 5 years and up to 7 years increased 66.0% to $128.5 billion, with on-the-run securities accounting for 81.9%. Those aggregates measure turnover rather than the direction of demand, but they show how much activity accompanied the auction and the broader rally.

The supply was absorbed against an unusually cash-rich funding backdrop. About $120 billion flowed into money-market funds during May, while repo rates traded below the lower bound of the Fed’s target range. The effective federal funds rate moved lower twice during the month, and the Secured Overnight Financing Rate was just above 3.50% after averaging roughly 3.65% in April.

Part of that softness came from the reduction of more than $270 billion in Treasury-bill supply around the April tax season and from Treasury cash-management buybacks, which left abundant cash competing for collateral. Strategists at several banks, however, judged the move too persistent to be explained by seasonal factors alone.

Changes to the enhanced supplementary leverage ratio have expanded the capacity of large banks to intermediate Treasury and repo positions. Some banks adopted the change before its April 1 deadline, helping dealers accommodate inventories even as their Treasury holdings reached a record $557 billion at the end of March. Wells Fargo has also become a large marginal provider of repo financing since its asset cap was removed in June 2025.

The scale of the balance-sheet expansion is substantial. Total assets at the eight U.S.-based global systemically important banks rose by a combined $1.3 trillion in the first quarter. Reverse-repo transactions accounted for $300 billion of that increase, while securities holdings grew by about $400 billion, including $100 billion in Treasury trading books. That additional intermediation capacity helps explain why heavy dealer inventories have not produced the funding strains seen last year.

Persistent softness could affect the Fed’s reserve-management purchases. Officials have already reduced monthly Treasury-bill buying to about $10 billion, from $40 billion through April and $25 billion in May. New York Fed markets chief Roberto Perli has said the pace can be adjusted to conditions, and strategists have raised the possibility of a pause if overnight funding remains unusually loose.

The funding environment is not merely a technical counterpoint to the Treasury rally. Lower repo costs make it easier for dealers to finance larger inventories and absorb supply, while a durable expansion of bank balance-sheet capacity reduces the likelihood that routine issuance produces a sudden collateral or reserve squeeze. The June cash-management operations will provide the next test of how those structural and seasonal influences interact.

## Credit Demand Is Strong, but It Is Becoming More Discriminating

European banks are exploiting tight risk premiums by extending the period before they can call Additional Tier 1 securities. Bonds with 10-year call dates account for one-quarter of major-currency AT1 issuance in 2026, an unprecedented share in a market where the standard first-call period has traditionally been 5 years.

Banco Santander sold $1.5 billion of non-call 10-year AT1 debt, while NatWest issued £500 million of securities callable in 2036 with a 7.5% coupon. Deutsche Bank, BNP Paribas and UBS have also issued long-call structures this year. Banks can secure roughly 10 years of Tier 1 funding at spreads of about 300 basis points because the spread curve between 5- and 10-year maturities is relatively flat and much of the incremental rates exposure can be swapped.

For investors, the structure carries more duration and liquidity risk than a conventional 5-year-call bond. Longer-call AT1s can fall more sharply if underlying rates rise, and the smaller secondary market may lose liquidity more quickly under stress. Tight new-issue spreads also leave less protection against repricing. The same extension can produce stronger upside when a bank’s equity improves, because the bond price is less tightly anchored to an expected redemption at par in the near term.

Demand is also supporting emerging-market borrowers that can offer insulation from sovereign political risk. Argentine provinces and Buenos Aires City issued a combined $2.3 billion during the first 5 months of 2026, the most for that period since 2017. Buenos Aires City raised $500 million through a 10-year bond at 7.4%, the lowest borrowing cost in its history, after attracting about $3 billion in orders.

Cordoba sold $800 million at 8.95% and Chubut raised $650 million at 9.45%, with both using the market to refinance debt and extend maturities. Chubut backed its bond with oil-royalty revenue. Entre Rios returned to international markets for the first time in nearly a decade with a $300 million deal at 9.6%.

The provincial market is offering investors a way to separate stronger local credits or secured revenue streams from the federal government’s election exposure. Argentina’s sovereign has stayed with short-term local debt and repo financing rather than issuing externally at yields near 9%. Local sovereign dollar bonds maturing before the 2027 election yielded roughly 5.1%, compared with about 8.6% for debt maturing afterward.

That distinction is useful but incomplete. Provinces generally need access to central-bank dollars to service foreign-currency obligations, and past sovereign crises have spread rapidly to local issuers. Provincial debt was restructured during both the 2001 collapse and the 2020 crisis, when Buenos Aires province reorganized almost all of its $7.1 billion of defaulted bonds.

Elsewhere in private markets, the largest proposed financings are increasingly being built around structural credit protection rather than the borrower’s standalone earnings. Apollo and Blackstone are seeking additional investors for roughly $36 billion of debt to fund chips that Anthropic will lease for artificial-intelligence infrastructure in New York, Texas, Louisiana and Indiana.

A special-purpose vehicle would buy Google-designed tensor processing units and receive Anthropic’s lease payments. The financing is expected to comprise about $6 billion of A1 notes, $25 billion of A2 notes and $4.5 billion of B notes, although the amounts remain subject to change. It uses a delayed-draw structure so capital can be advanced as chips become available and leases begin.

Broadcom, which helps Google develop the chips, would provide residual-value support to the senior A1 and A2 notes. If Anthropic stopped making lease payments for a specified period, the vehicle would sell the chips. Broadcom would cover any shortfall required to repay those senior investors in full, aligning their credit profile with Broadcom’s investment-grade standing while leaving the junior B notes below them in the repayment structure.

The protection is central because Anthropic does not yet generate the earnings needed to support debt of this size on its own. The company separately announced a $65 billion equity round at a $965 billion valuation. Apollo and Blackstone intend to retain substantial portions of the financing while syndicating the rest, with orders sought during the week and completion expected the following week.

The contrast with software refinancing is stark. Several private-credit firms declined to participate in Thoma Bravo’s proposed $2.5 billion refinancing of cybersecurity company Sophos even after the indicated spread rose to nearly 600 basis points over the benchmark rate. Sophos’s existing debt pays about 350 basis points over and includes a $2.1 billion loan maturing in March 2027.

Thoma Bravo is consequently considering a parallel amendment-and-extension process with Goldman Sachs. Existing lenders are seeking additional sponsor equity, a partial repayment of debt and higher pricing in exchange for extending maturity by roughly 2.5 years. Thoma Bravo already has more than $2.3 billion of equity invested in the company.

S&P Global Ratings recently lowered the outlook on a Sophos entity to negative and said the rating could be cut if the coming maturities were not refinanced within 2 months. Sophos’s loan traded near 97 cents, and the company generated free cash flow in its December quarter with annual recurring revenue of about $1.34 billion. Those operating and market indicators provide support, but the compressed refinancing timetable has become a liquidity constraint.

The resistance reflects a broader reassessment of software exposure as lenders consider whether artificial intelligence could weaken established subscription businesses. Some business-development companies have begun selling selected software loans, while other investors are buying discounted positions. The difference between the Anthropic and Sophos transactions shows that appetite for technology-related private debt remains large when the structure transfers key risk to a stronger balance sheet, but is far less automatic when lenders must underwrite the borrower’s refinancing and disruption risk directly.

A separate dispute at Jefferies underscored the legal and collateral risks in less-liquid credit. Investors in Leucadia Asset Management’s 352 Capital fund filed a proposed class action alleging that the fund continued buying Water Station Management bonds despite knowledge that collateral did not exist and that former portfolio manager Jordan Chirico had a personal investment in the business.

Jefferies has alleged that Chirico misled it about his investments and relationship with Water Station. Chirico, who pleaded not guilty after being charged with fraud, has said through counsel that he was a victim rather than an organizer of the alleged scheme. The investor complaint seeks unspecified damages and alleges that bond-document protections, including events of default tied to collateral representations and financial reporting, were waived. Those remain allegations rather than adjudicated findings.

## Central Banks Confront the Energy Shock

The European Central Bank’s account of its April 29-30 meeting showed that a number of officials regarded the decision as close and would not have opposed a rate increase had one been formally proposed. Policymakers have since indicated that an increase is likely in June, including some officials normally associated with the dovish side of the Governing Council.

Euro-area inflation was running at 3%, and officials were concerned that higher energy costs could pass into wage demands and longer-term expectations. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane said that even if the initial energy shock reversed, its second-round effects would persist for some time. Economists and investors expected at least two increases during 2026.

South Africa acted immediately. The South African Reserve Bank raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 7%, its first increase since 2023 and in line with the forecast of 18 of 19 surveyed economists. The six-member committee split 4-2, with two members preferring no change, after also discussing a 50-basis-point increase.

Governor Lesetja Kganyago said intensified inflation risks and overlapping shocks could generate second-round effects. All three of the central bank’s war scenarios implied some further tightening, with the most adverse path putting the policy rate at 7.83% by the third quarter. The bank raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 4.4% from 3.7%, lowered its growth estimate to 1.2% from 1.4%, and lifted the year-end rate projection in its quarterly model to 6.7% from 6.47%.

South African inflation accelerated to 4.0% in April from 3.1%, its highest in 20 months, after fuel prices reached an almost 4-year high. The rand remained about 0.2% stronger at 16.327 per dollar late in Johannesburg after paring an earlier gain, while the 10-year government yield reversed a selloff and fell to 8.62%, 9 basis points below its session high.

Brazil, by contrast, is reassessing whether an easing cycle can continue. Central-bank Monetary Policy Director Nilton David highlighted the worsening of 2028 inflation expectations after the bank delivered two consecutive 25-basis-point cuts. Annual inflation accelerated to 4.64% in early May, and some economists expected the bank to pause as soon as June with the Selic rate at 14.5%.

David said policy could do little to change 2026 inflation but still had time to bring expectations for 2028 back toward the 3% target. The comments made clear that lower rates did not represent a shift away from restrictive policy and that an external energy shock would not be allowed to propagate beyond the relevant policy horizon, currently the fourth quarter of 2027.

## Europe and Japan Reprice Sovereign Duration

Europe’s debate over common borrowing is moving closer to the center of fiscal policy as governments confront defense, infrastructure and energy-transition costs. A paper signed by 16 member states in late May called for consideration of new joint borrowing to support loans for European investment and public goods. It also advocated a more gradual repayment schedule for pandemic-recovery debt, whose repayments are due to begin in 2028.

France, Spain and Greece broadly support more common issuance, while Germany and the Netherlands remain wary of mutualizing fiscal obligations. The European Commission has proposed targeted instruments financed through common borrowing, including a crisis facility of as much as €400 billion. Poland has backed joint debt for defense, and Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel has said some national borrowing capacity could move to the EU level.

The outstanding pandemic recovery facility exceeds €800 billion, and the bloc has separately agreed to a €90 billion loan to Ukraine backed by the EU budget. A defense-loan program adopted in 2025 already allows the Commission to borrow and then lend to national governments, keeping repayment obligations with the individual member states.

At sufficient scale, common issuance could create a deeper euro-area safe asset alongside German Bunds, broaden banks’ sovereign exposures and provide a more liquid benchmark for private borrowing. Alternatives include sovereign bond-backed securities, which would pool national debt as collateral and create tranches with different risk and yield without adding mutual obligations. Both approaches depend on issuance volume to produce meaningful liquidity, while permanent joint borrowing would require political agreement that does not yet exist.

Japan is already showing how a structural rise in sovereign yields can reshape an entire financial system. The 10-year Japanese government-bond yield has climbed above the Topix dividend yield for the first time since 2008. The yield on Japanese corporate bonds has reached the highest level since the relevant index began in 2000, raising refinancing costs as older liabilities mature.

The move is no longer being read solely as healthy normalization after the Bank of Japan ended negative rates in 2024. Daiwa Securities estimated that the term premium on 10-year JGBs had risen almost 70 basis points since the Iran war began. The yen weakened even as yields rose, suggesting that investors were attaching more weight to inflation, fiscal expansion and heavier government supply than to a straightforward improvement in returns on Japanese assets.

Tokyo inflation data released during the Asian morning after the U.S. close complicated the BOJ’s June decision. Consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 1.3% from a year earlier in May, the slowest pace in 4 years and a sixth consecutive deceleration. Inflation excluding fresh food and energy was 1.6%, while headline CPI was 1.4%.

Government subsidies and a steep decline in water-service fees restrained the index. Service prices rose 1.1%, and food excluding fresh items increased 4.1%; rice prices fell 1.0%, their first decline since August 2022. Industrial production unexpectedly rose in April, retail sales strengthened from March and unemployment declined to 2.5%.

Those results softened the current inflation picture without removing the oil, currency and fiscal risks facing the BOJ. Traders assigned roughly a 77% probability to a 25-basis-point increase at the June 15-16 meeting. The yen was near 159.31 per dollar, close to its weakest level since the April 30 currency intervention, while announced food-price increases for August pointed to continuing pass-through pressure.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. growth update arrives on May 29 with the April advance economic indicators. Consensus estimates put the goods-trade deficit at $86.5 billion, compared with $87.9 billion previously, with retail inventories expected to rise 0.4% and wholesale inventories 0.8%. Those inputs will affect tracking estimates after the downward revision to first-quarter GDP.

The June 1 ISM manufacturing survey will test whether the 52.7 reading in April was followed by continued expansion. New orders and employment will help determine whether the weakness in core capital-goods orders is broadening, while prices paid will show whether the energy shock is spreading through industrial inputs.

Labor evidence then becomes more detailed. April JOLTS data on June 2 will update openings, hires and quits after an initially reported 6.866 million vacancies. The May ADP report follows at 08:15 ET on June 3, after a prior 109,000 increase, and another initial-claims reading arrives June 4 after the rise to 215,000. Together they will show whether the latest claims increase was noise or the beginning of a softer labor-flow trend.

The June 3 ISM services survey is the more consequential growth-inflation cross-check after PCE. The previous headline reading was 53.6, but the employment and prices-paid components will matter most for a Fed debating whether to remove its easing bias. The Beige Book later that day will add district-level evidence on demand, hiring, credit conditions and price pressure ahead of the June 17-18 FOMC meeting.

Treasury operations will also test the unusually loose funding environment. A June 3 liquidity-support buyback may accept as much as $2.0 billion of 20- to 30-year nominal coupons between 13:40 and 14:00 ET, with settlement on June 4. A June 4 cash-management buyback may accept up to $12.5 billion of 1-month to 2-year nominal coupons, settling June 5. The former is a scheduled long-duration liquidity operation; the latter has more direct implications for the supply of short-maturity collateral and the cash-rich repo market.

section_summaries.summary: Longer-dated Treasuries led a bull-flattening rally as weaker demand data reduced real-rate pressure. The 10-year real yield fell 3.5 basis points while the breakeven slipped only 0.1 basis point, and a well-received $44 billion 7-year auction supported the move. Elevated annual inflation and disagreement within the Fed kept the close from signaling an unambiguous disinflation turn.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally and the curve flattens as softer demand lowers real yields without easing inflation concern
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied across the curve, led by longer maturities. The 10-year yield fell 3.6 basis points to 4.448% and the 30-year declined 3.9 basis points to 4.974%, while the 2-year eased 1.1 basis points to 4.023%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 2.5 basis points to 42.5 basis points.

The move followed softer household income, a downward revision in Q1 growth, weaker core capital-goods orders and a sharp new-home-sales miss. Monthly core PCE inflation was also softer than expected at 0.2%, but annual headline and core inflation remained elevated at 3.8% and 3.3%. The 10-year real yield accounted for almost the entire nominal-yield decline, while the breakeven was nearly unchanged, indicating less real-rate pressure rather than a material reduction in the inflation premium. Strong demand at the $44 billion 7-year auction reinforced the rally.

Fed officials offered conflicting interpretations of the outlook. John Williams described policy as slightly restrictive and well placed to wait, while Alberto Musalem argued that the real policy rate was below neutral and kept a rate increase under consideration. Futures assigned more than a 50% probability to an increase by year-end. Equities advanced and volatility declined alongside bonds, while Brent’s weekly fall reduced the immediate energy impulse without removing concern about second-round inflation.
overall_summary.summary: Softer income, underlying investment, housing and Q1 growth pulled 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields lower, while sticky annual inflation and a divided Fed debate prevented the rally from becoming a clean disinflation signal.
